blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Citizenship Act of 1955 defines the legal pathways to obtain Indian citizenship.
Citizenship can be acquired natively through Birth or Descent.
Individuals can apply for citizenship via Registration or Naturalisation.
When a new territory becomes part of India, citizenship is granted through Incorporation of Territory.
Memorize all 5 methods of acquisition: Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, and Incorporation of Territory.
Questions often ask to identify which option is NOT a valid method of acquiring citizenship under the 1955 Act.
